findings.title: A reifier node always lands in the default graph, and erasing the edge's graph leaves it (with its properties) live
findings.intended: Erasure removes a graph's content from every store (SYS-D26, ADR-0004); content of one graph never shows up in an answer about another graph (SYS-I2); INT-E1.6/INT-E1.7 (a reifier lives with its edge and goes with its graph).
findings.observed: Live (c15-live-reify): reify_edge on an edge of named graph c15g1 wrote the reifier node, its label 'Reification' and its properties with graph_id '' (default graph) in one transaction; the edge is in c15g1. erase_graph('c15g1') deleted the edge and its rdf_reifications row (journal: one transaction) but the reifier node, label and properties {'source': 'tenant-c15g1-secret', 'confidence': 0.9} stayed in the default graph and were returned by get_node('c15:reif1') and by a default-graph Cypher MATCH. delete_node removes the reifiers of a node's edges (INT-E1.9), so the two deletion paths disagree. The FHIR sync's DeleteEdge (FHIRGraph.cls:2585-2599) also deletes only the rdf_reifications link, never the reifier node.
findings.remedy: Create the reifier in the edge's graph (read graph_id with edge_id) and have every edge-deleting path (Eraser.EraseGraph/EraseNodes, FHIR sync DeleteEdge, direct and Cypher edge deletes) delete the reifier nodes of the edges it removes, in the same transaction; a live test that reifies an edge in G, erases G and finds no reifier in any graph.

findings.notes: Original 'leaves its edges and adjacency without a node row' is not reproducible on a fresh install: the edge FKs exist (they are dropped and re-added by the 3.x->4 graph_id migration, schema.py:1436-1510, so an install whose migration stopped between those steps could still show it).
findings.title: delete_reification deletes any id's node, labels and properties in every graph without checking it is a reifier
findings.intended: SYS-I2 (graph isolation) and INT-E1.10 ('deleting a reifier should touch only that reifier node, and leave no edge without its node'); the docstring (schema.py:3364-3368) admits 'Not graph-scoped'.
findings.observed: Live (c15-live-delreif2): delete_reification('c15:z') on an id that is no reifier (0 rdf_reifications rows) and has no edges deleted its node row, labels, properties and ^KG('label') index entries in BOTH named graph c15g2b and the default graph, in one transaction, and returned True. Sub-claim refuted at the pin (c15-live-delreif): for an id WITH edges the foreign key fk_edges_source (schema.py:42) refuses the node delete (SQLCODE -124) and the whole transaction rolls back, so no edge is left without its node row and ^KG is unchanged; the call raises GraphWriteError naming the FK.
findings.remedy: Refuse an id with no rdf_reifications row; scope the deletes to the reifier's graph (the default graph at the pin, or the edge's graph once F-1502 is fixed).

findings.title: map_sql_table looks up an unqualified table in schema 'USER' instead of the default schema SQLUser
findings.intended: INT-M1.4: a table name with no schema is found in the default SQL schema; IRIS puts an unqualified table in SQLUser (P-1509).
findings.observed: Live (c15-live-tablemap): %SYSTEM.SQL.Schema.Default() = 'SQLUser'; INFORMATION_SCHEMA has 0 tables in schema 'USER'; the catalog query map_sql_table runs for an unqualified name uses TABLE_SCHEMA='USER' (fhir.py:113-120) and so refuses every unqualified name ('Table ... not found'), while the qualified IVGAudit.C15Patients mapping succeeds. A real SQLUser table mapped unqualified was not driven: AUDITC has no SQLUser table and the audit may create scratch tables only under IVGAudit.*.
findings.remedy: Use the namespace default schema (SQLUser, or $SYSTEM.SQL.Schema.Default()) for an unqualified name; add a test with an unqualified table.

findings.notes: Model (main lane, explorer, exhaustive within bounds): as-built violates 'a refused register changes nothing' (upsert committed before LoadColumns throws); the links-change path reports 'rebuild pending' as documented (FHIRGraph.cls:262-271, pass); the reviewed design passes and its upsert-outside-transaction control is caught. Live reproduction is blocked-access: HS.FHIRServer.* classes and the HS_FHIRServer SQL schema (an IRIS for Health FHIR repository) are absent on IRIS Community 2026.1 in AUDITC: 0 classes, 0 tables, Register answers 'no FHIR repository' (live c15-live-register).
findings.title: A register that fails after its upsert keeps the new settings
findings.intended: SYS-I3 (a refused command leaves every store as it was); INT-F3.9.
findings.observed: Source: Register upserts Graph_KG.fhir_graphs (FHIRGraph.cls:235-245) with autocommit Exec and no TSTART, then runs Open, LoadColumns (LoadLinks, LoadCompartment, LoadProps, HS.FHIRServer.Schema.LoadSchema) and the json_links UPDATE (:247-258); the Catch (:276-278) returns an error without undoing the upsert. Live on Community (c15-live-register): every refusal reachable without a repository happens before the upsert and wrote 0 journal records, so the defect window cannot be entered here.
findings.model_hint: as-built: Register = [validate] -> upsert settings (autocommit) -> Open/LoadColumns may throw -> json_links UPDATE; a throw after the upsert returns error with new settings stored (violates 'refused => stores unchanged'). reviewed (decisions SYS-I3/INT-F3.9): validate and load columns first, then upsert + json_links in one transaction, so a refusal changes nothing. Negative control: reviewed with the upsert moved before validation must be caught.
findings.remedy: Validate and load metadata before writing, then do the upsert and the json_links update in one transaction (or roll back the upsert on failure).

findings.notes: Found by the footprint pass (footprints/15.json). Matters for durable tenant removal (HD-1502): an orphan task keeps re-filling an erased FHIR graph after a 'successful' unschedule.
findings.title: Schedule/Unschedule change the Task Manager task and the fhir_graphs task_id in separate, untransacted steps
findings.intended: SYS-I4 (a command that writes to more than one store writes all or none); INT-F9 (one sync task per graph); HD-1502 reviewed design needs an unschedule that verifiably stops refills.
findings.observed: Source: Schedule saves the %SYS.Task (FHIRGraph.cls:701, %Save) and only then records its id with a separate autocommit UPDATE Graph_KG.fhir_graphs SET task_id (:703); Unschedule deletes the task (:726) and then clears task_id (:729). No TSTART covers either pair. If the UPDATE fails after Schedule's %Save, a running sync task exists that fhir_graphs does not name: Unschedule then reports success without removing it, and the next Schedule creates a second task. Not run live: HS.FHIRServer.* classes and the HS_FHIRServer SQL schema (an IRIS for Health FHIR repository) are absent on IRIS Community 2026.1 in AUDITC: 0 classes, 0 tables, Register answers 'no FHIR repository' (live c15-live-register).
findings.remedy: Wrap the task change and the task_id update in one transaction (IRIS transactions span the IRISSYS and namespace databases), or make Unschedule find tasks by (TaskClass, NameSpace, GraphId) rather than by the stored id.

findings.title: delete_node removes the reifier nodes of the node's edges in a second transaction
findings.intended: SYS-I4 (all or none across stores); INT-E1.9 (deleting a node also deletes the reifier nodes of its edges).
findings.observed: Live (c15-live-reify, delete_node_parity): delete_node('c15:a2', graph='c15g1b') journaled two outermost transactions: the node, its edge and the rdf_reifications row in the first, the reifier node c15:reif2 (default graph) in the second. _delete_in_scope (nodes_edges.py:2176-2199) deletes reifiers after the node delete commits and, on failure, raises GraphWriteError 'the node is deleted; the reifier nodes of its edges (n) are not'.
findings.remedy: Delete the reifier nodes inside the same transaction as the node and its edges.
